Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-03-06):
- History: Prices have been declining from ~83 down to ~68.5 over 18 days
- Model forecasts: Also declining from ~67.4, but they're too high
- True outcomes: Also declining, but faster and further - ending around 60-66 range vs model's 67-70

Looking at Example 2 (2025-03-05):
- Very similar to Example 1, just one day earlier
- Model forecasts are again too high (starting at 68.83 vs true 68.79, but diverge significantly)
- True outcomes are about 2-4 points lower than model forecasts for the first 15 days
- After day 15, both converge as prices continue falling

Example 3 (2025-01-20):
- History: Prices have been rising from ~68.2 up to ~79.3 over 18 days
- Model forecasts: Also rising, but too low! (starting at 79.84 vs true 79.99+)
- Wait, let me look more carefully... the model forecasts are slightly below true outcomes for the first 10 days or so
- But then the divergence becomes more pronounced

Example 4 (2025-01-17):
- Same history as Example 3 (just one day earlier)
- Model forecasts again slightly below true outcomes for the first 10-12 days
- Then they converge as the divergence grows

Example 5 (2025-01-21):
- History matches Example 3
- Model forecasts again lower than true outcomes for the first 10 days
- Then convergence
